title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look? Some of the variance you measured here may now have a mechanism.

Your six-run table showed buckets moving on identical code with the total exactly conserved (4,702 every time), `known-fp` going `2 / 1 / 0 / 2 / 0 / 0`, and `authzPrecondition` co-varying inversely with `clean`. Your stated hypothesis was Akto's own per-run auth-context setup, flagged explicitly as untested.

**A second variable was present in every one of those runs and was invisible to the instrument.** Under KS-709 we found that Akto records an HTTP 429 as a *completed result carrying no error*, so a rate-limited test matched no branch of our classifier and fell through its `default:"clean"`. Measured on slot 2, 2026-09-28, full OWASP run `6aba139ce86558333055a8f9`: **8,735 of 50,018 results were 429s, 0 had any error, and all 8,735 sat in `clean`** — 79% of that run's entire clean bucket, under a verdict of PASS.

That is consistent with the shape you recorded: throttling is load- and timing-dependent, so it moves run to run; the total is conserved because the results still exist and are still counted; and it lands precisely in `clean`, the bucket you saw absorbing the movement.

**I am not claiming it explains your variance** — your runs were on a different commit and a different tier, `known-fp` movement is a detection difference that throttling does not obviously produce, and I have not re-run your six. It is a candidate that was not on the table when you measured, and it was unmeasurable then because the bucket did not exist.

`rateLimited` is now a first-class bucket, so a repeat of your six-run experiment would separate the two axes for the first time. That seems worth doing before anyone pays for the auth-context instrumentation you identified as the next step.

Your standing rule from this ticket — **"compare failing sets, never counts"** — is carried unchanged; nothing here weakens it.

## BLUF

**Re-measured on the fixed harness: six runs on one frozen commit, all with healthy captures. The variance is real — but this ticket's headline figure was partly an artifact of [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700), and I need to correct my own s79 conclusion.**

## 🔴 Correction — s79's `2 / 0 / 2` middle term was never measured

The three-run table on this ticket records `countIssues.HIGH` as **2 / 0 / 2** and concludes *"the platform never changes its answer; Akto changes its verdict."*

Run 2 of that set — `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-03Z` — is **the run whose Mongo capture failed**. It is the exact run KS-700 was filed about. Verified directly in its artifact just now: `skipBreakdown` is **absent**, so no bucket data was ever recorded, and its "0" is the false zero, not a measurement.

The two runs in that set that *did* measure agreed **exactly**:

| s79 run | known-fp | clean | authz-precondition | total |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `11-27-28Z` | 2 | 804 | 255 | 4702 |
| `11-28-03Z` | — | — | — | **CAPTURE FAILED — nothing measured** |
| `11-28-50Z` | 2 | 804 | 257 | 4702 |

So the evidence s79 offered for non-determinism was two runs that agreed and one that did not report. **The conclusion happened to be right — the new data below shows real variance — but it was not supported by the data it was drawn from.** This is exactly the failure mode KS-700 describes: a capture failure is indistinguishable from a measurement, and it got read as one.

## New measurement — 6 runs, one commit, all captures healthy

Commit `2e3800a71`, stack untouched, runs 20–40 s apart, `testResultsCount` = **4702** every time:

| run | known-fp | clean | connectivity | authz-precondition | not-applicable | total | capture |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | **2** | 803 | 1 | 257 | 3279 | 4702 | OK |
| 2 | **1** | 806 | 1 | 253 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 3 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 251 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 4 | **2** | 804 | 0 | 255 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 5 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 251 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 6 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 253 | 3279 | 4702 | OK |

**The variance is confirmed: `2 / 1 / 0 / 2 / 0 / 0`.** Every run: verdict PASS, `vulnerable 0`, and the flagged endpoints are always the same two — `GET /api/identity-credentials/types` and `GET /api/oauth/scopes`, both `REMOVE_TOKENS`, both caught by the endpoint-scoped FP register (hence known-fp rather than vulnerable).

### Three things the six runs establish that three could not

1. **It is not warming.** Runs 1→3 declined 2→1→0, which looks like accumulated state — and then run 4 went back to **2**. A three-run window would have supported a warming hypothesis that six runs refute.
2. **The total is exactly conserved.** 4702 in all six, and the per-bucket sums reconcile to it every time. Results **move between buckets**; none are lost. So this is a classification difference, not a coverage difference.
3. **`clean` tracks the flag inversely and `authzPrecondition` co-varies.** known-fp 2 → clean 803–804; known-fp 0 → clean 810. `authzPrecondition` moves 251–257 across the same runs.

### What that points at (hypothesis, not a finding)

The co-variation of `authzPrecondition` with the flag suggests the variable is **Akto's own per-run auth-context setup**, not its detection logic: when more results execute cleanly, fewer land in the authz-precondition bucket and the no-auth template has a different baseline to compare against. s79 established the platform side is stable — both endpoints answered **200 unauthenticated, 20/20**, with controls firing.

**I have not tested this.** It is the next thing to measure, and it needs a run that records Akto's auth setup per run, which the harness does not currently capture.

## Status of the KS-700 blocker

s79 recorded KS-700 as blocking this ticket's root cause. Partly cleared: the six runs above all captured successfully, so the false zero **did not recur** and this data is trustworthy. But that also means run 2 of s79 — the one run that would have told us what a divergent run looks like from the inside — remains unexplained, and the false zero is **intermittent**, so it can still corrupt a future measurement. The KS-700 fix (PR [#752](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/752)) makes such a run **fail loudly** rather than report zeros, which is what makes measurements like this one safe to trust going forward.

---

*Measured 2026-08-27, session 80, on the KS-700 branch. Read-only against the local stack; demo untouched.*

## BLUF

**Measured: three `test:pr` runs on a frozen commit and an untouched stack, 35–47 s apart. Akto's own issue count came back 2 / 0 / 2 — and the platform answers those endpoints identically 20/20.** So the variance is inside Akto's verdict engine: not the code under test, not the platform, and not our reporting.

**Two further things fell out, and both change what this ticket is about:**

1. **"No captured request" is ours, not Akto's.** Akto captured a full request+response for **every** flagged result — verified directly in Mongo (3,030–46,378 characters of `testResults[0].message`). Our report says `request: null` and prints a placeholder curl reading *"Akto returned no captured request for this result"*. The data is one field away from the report.
2. 🔴 **The harness can fail its capture silently and then print a FALSE ZERO.** Run 2 emitted `throughput: 0 results (0 executed) in 36s — no executed requests`. Mongo says run 2 executed **4,702** results. Nothing was logged at default level. Filed separately as **KS-700**.

## Recommendation

Fix the capture before chasing the engine. Two of the three problems here are ours and are cheap; the Akto-engine variance is real but is the expensive one, and it cannot be triaged while findings arrive without a reproducer.

## Detail — the three runs (item 1's ask)

Commit `cd52a6a7a` (#751's head — the running `originate` container was built from it at 11:00:30Z, two minutes after the commit). Stack untouched between runs: 37 containers, 0 unhealthy. All three runs `state=COMPLETED`, `testResultsCount=4702`, 4,702 docs in Mongo.

| run | wall | Akto `countIssues.HIGH` | flagged results in Mongo | identity | captured request **in Mongo** | captured request **in our report** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-27-28Z` | 19.2 s | **2** | 2 | `REMOVE_TOKENS` `/api/oauth/scopes` · `REMOVE_TOKENS` `/api/identity-credentials/types` | yes — 3,526 / 3,031 chars | **none captured** |
| 2 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-03Z` | 39.8 s | **0** | 0 | — | n/a | **none captured** + every rich field `null` |
| 3 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-50Z` | 29.8 s | **2** | 2 | the same two | yes — 3,030 / 3,527 chars | **none captured** |

Runs 1 and 3 reported `verdict: PASS` because both findings are known-FPs; run 2 reported PASS with no bucket data at all. **All three PASS — for three different reasons.**

Bucket detail also moved between runs 1 and 3, conserving the total: `authzPrecondition` 255 → 257 and `byDesignFilter` 3281 → 3279. Two results changed classification on identical input.

### The discriminator: the platform is deterministic, Akto is not

`REMOVE_TOKENS` strips auth and checks whether data still comes back. Both flipping endpoints, probed unauthenticated 20 times each:

```
/api/oauth/scopes               200 ×20
/api/identity-credentials/types 200 ×20
controls: /api/documents 401 ×5   ·   /health 200 ×5
```

The controls discriminate. The platform's answer **never changes**, yet Akto flags these two in runs 1 and 3 and not in run 2. Both are intentionally-public reference endpoints, unrelated to #751's diff — so nothing about the code under test is involved.

**Per Wednesday's discriminator rule: no run flagged a route #751 touches (`transfer-custody` / `/api/documents`), so the extra clean-`develop` run was not required and was not done.**

### Root cause — stated as a HYPOTHESIS, not a result

**Not established.** What the evidence supports and does not:

- **Supports a timing/load-sensitivity hypothesis:** engine execution time varied 4× on identical work (`exec 3s` run 1 vs `exec 13s` run 3), and run 2 — the zero-finding run — had the longest wall clock (39.8 s).
- **Argues against it:** runs 1 and 3 differ by that same 4× and produced the *identical* finding set. So slower does not simply mean fewer findings.
- **Cannot be evaluated:** run 2's `engineTiming` is `null` (its capture failed), so the one run that matters most has no engine breakdown. That is a direct consequence of KS-700 — **the reporting gap is currently blocking the root-cause analysis.**

### KS-698 poisoning tested as a hypothesis — REFUTED

Asked whether KS-698's rate-limit poisoning could drive this. **It cannot**, and the first probe was inconclusive before it was refuted properly:

| probe | result | reading |
| -- | -- | -- |
| poisoned key, **no** bearer | 401 | inconclusive — never reached the handler |
| fresh key, **no** bearer (control) | 401 | **control agreed with the null → instrument not discriminating** |
| poisoned key, bearer | **500** ×2 | poisoning is live and still persistent ~40 min on |
| fresh key + valid `windowMs`, bearer (control) | **200** ×2 | control discriminates |

So KS-698 reproduces and persists — but the flipping findings are on two endpoints that are not the rate-limit route and that answer identically 20/20, so poisoning is not the mechanism here. Recording the first, non-discriminating probe because a control that agrees with the null is the signature that says suspect the instrument.

## Where the captured request is lost

`fetchRunResults` (`src/client/aktoTestRuns.ts:161`) POSTs to Akto's REST `/api/fetchTestingRunResults`, and that response carries the result documents **without** their `testResults[]` array — so `parseFinding` (`src/client/findingParser.ts:38`) reads `attempt.message ?? attempt.originalMessage` on an empty object and sets `request: null`.

The harness already knows this path is lossy. `src/report/resultsCapture.ts` says so in its own module docstring:

> *"Akto's REST `fetchTestingRunResults` is paginated, queryMode-segmented, and routed to a vulnerable-only collection — so for a clean run it returns nothing... All per-test detail, however, lives plainly in MongoDB."*

That module reads Mongo directly and is where the buckets/matrix/known-FP rows come from — but it derives **counts and classification only**, and never reads `testResults[].message`. So the reproducer is available in the same collection the rich capture already queries, one field away.

**Suggested fix direction (not built this session, per scope):** have `captureRunResults` project `testResults[0].message` for flagged results and use it to populate `request`/`response`, so `buildCurl` produces a real reproducer instead of the placeholder. That makes an Akto FAIL re-derivable by hand, which is the precondition for ever comparing finding *sets* on this gate the way we now do on Schemathesis.

## What this does to the merge gate

Two of tonight's three runs would have produced different bucket evidence on identical code, and one produced none at all while still reading PASS. Combined with KS-700, an Akto PASS currently means one of: nothing was flagged · things were flagged and reclassified as known-FP · or the capture failed and the run reported zeros it never measured. **Those three are not distinguishable from the console line**, which is the practical problem for the four-suite rule.

---

*Measured 2026-08-27, session 79. Runs on `cd52a6a7a`; artifacts under `systemTest/akto/output/reports/pr-2026-08-27T11-2*`. Read-only against Mongo; nothing merged, no deploy, demo untouched.*

## Schemathesis varies run-to-run too — but for the OPPOSITE reason, and the distinction matters

Not the measurement this ticket asks for (three Akto runs with capture on) — that is still to do. This is a finding from the same night that changes what this ticket is comparing against.

**Three Schemathesis `pr` runs on the same base commit gave three different failing sets:**

| run | count | set |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pr-2026-08-27T10-12-12Z` | 9 | the KS-693 floor |
| `pr-2026-08-27T10-29-58Z` | 10 | floor **+ transfer-custody** (found KS-697) |
| `pr-2026-08-27T11-04-05Z` | 10 | floor **− transfer-custody + rate-limit/check** |

So **two of the four merge gates now vary run-to-run.** But they are not the same problem and should not be fixed as one:

| | Akto (this ticket) | Schemathesis |
| -- | -- | -- |
| varies across runs | yes — 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH / 0 HIGH | yes — 9 / 10 / 10 |
| **captured request** | **none** | **yes, replayable** |
| reproduces on demand | **no** | **100%** |
| what the variance means | the harness cannot show its work | the harness is doing its job on a latent bug |

The Schemathesis variance is **stochastic discovery of a deterministic defect** — Hypothesis has to generate a body that clears validation *and* carries an out-of-range value. Once it does, the captured curl reproduces every time. That is a working fuzzer, not a broken one. (The defect it found is now [KS-698](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-698) — one request permanently poisons a rate-limit key.)

Akto's variance has no captured request behind it, so there is nothing to replay and no way to tell a real finding from a phantom. **That is the thing this ticket should fix**, and it is a harness problem, not a platform one.

## Consequence for the merge gate, worth stating plainly

**"Schemathesis FAIL 9, byte-identical to baseline" is a weaker claim than it reads** — and it is the phrasing used on several PRs today, mine among them. A count is not a signature. The *set* of failing operations is, and only the set showed that the KS-697 fix had landed: this branch also scored 10, the same number as the run that found the bug.

Suggest the same rule lands on both gates: **compare failing sets, never counts.** For Akto that is blocked until findings carry a captured request — which is this ticket.
